changelog:
[COLOR fffdb515]The add-on decides how your content is laid out, not the skin[/COLOR]
-Films, shows, seasons and episodes were only pushed into a poster wall on Estuary and Confluence, because those were the only two view numbers written into the code. Every other skin was left to its own default, usually a plain list, which is why the add-on looked like a different add-on depending on the skin.
-The wall is now read out of the skin itself instead of being guessed, so it works on any skin. Checked against Estuary, Estuary MOD V2, Confluence and Aeon Nox: SiLVO, each of which uses a different number for the same layout. The answer is remembered, and if a skin tries to put its own view back a moment later it is set again.
-You stay in charge. Set Add-on View under Tools still wins over everything, and that screen now opens in the view you already have rather than the one the add-on would impose. There is a switch in settings to turn the whole thing off.
[COLOR fffdb515]Trending and Popular are ready before you open them[/COLOR]
-Trending and Popular are the first two entries in Movies and TV shows and neither was ever precached, because they come from Trakt and the start-up refresh only spoke to TMDb. Both are warmed up now. Meanwhile the refresh was spending its time on two film lists the menu does not even show, so every list is now precached only if its menu entry is switched on.
-Start-up work comes in three parts. First, on its own: Trending, Popular, In Theaters and the platforms and channels you picked by hand. Then in the background, capped at thirty seconds: Top Rated, Upcoming, Box Office, Airing Today and On The Air. Last, the weekly rota over everything you did not pick, which now runs at every start-up.
-The first part no longer shares its time allowance with the other two, so a slow night for TMDb can trim the background work but never what you see first. Widgets refresh as soon as that first part is done. Measured on an Android tablet: twenty-five lists ready in under five seconds.
[COLOR fffdb515]The background artwork queue no longer falls behind[/COLOR]
-Lists appear quickly because the finishing touches - channel logos, alternative posters - are filled in afterwards, a few titles at a time. On a home screen built out of add-on widgets that queue grew about as fast as it was emptied and could sit in the hundreds indefinitely. It now works on four titles at once in larger batches and comes back every ten seconds while there is a queue. A backlog of seven hundred titles that previously never cleared is now gone in under four minutes.
-It still stops the moment you start watching something, and it still steps back to its normal pace when nothing is being completed, so an outage cannot turn it into a loop.
-The rota over the remaining platforms and channels was only allowed to run once that queue was completely empty, which on a busy home screen meant never. It keeps its own schedule now.
